Two such fields exist: `IMMDATES-PGM-NAME` (declared once in copybook COPYBOOKS/IMMDATED.CPY, PIC X(08) VALUE 'IMMDATES', pulled in via plain `COPY IMMDATED.` with no REPLACING in every including program, so the field name is never renamed) and a locally-declared `WS-IMMDATES` (PIC X(08) VALUE 'IMMDATES') redeclared independently in 9 programs (2 of which ΓÇö IMM0046, IMM0680 ΓÇö declare it but never actually CALL it, so they're excluded as non-calls). Searched for `CALL IMMDATES-PGM-NAME` (232 files, 572 call sites) and `CALL WS-IMMDATES` (7 files, 23 call sites) as executable code.

Read COPYBOOKS/IMMDATED.CPY, which is COPYed by nearly all callers and defines IMMDATES-PARM with field IMMDATES-PGM-NAME PIC X(08) VALUE 'IMMDATES' ΓÇö this is the field used in the indirect call pattern "CALL IMMDATES-PGM-NAME USING IMMDATES-PARM". A separate grep for VALUE 'IMMDATES'/VALUE "IMMDATES" found a second, locally-declared field name (WS-IMMDATES) used identically in 7 programs that don't rely on the copybook field, confirmed via a targeted "CALL WS-IMMDATES" grep. Literal CALL 'IMMDATES' USING IMMDATES-PARM statements were identified directly in the content grep. Comment-only occurrences (COBOL '*' comment lines, DISPLAY string literals, and documentation text inside IMMDATED.CPY) were excluded from the call count ΓÇö notably IMM9430.COB, whose only match is a commented-out CALL line, was excluded entirely. Each of the ~625 matching source lines was manually classified as call vs. non-call and by call_style, then deduplicated to file level (a file with both literal and indirect calls appears as two entries). (1) Literal `CALL 'IMMDATES' USING IMMDATES-PARM` ΓÇö 11 files.
(2) Indirect calls via `IMMDATES-PGM-NAME`, a PIC X(08) field defined once in COPYBOOKS/IMMDATED.CPY with `VALUE 'IMMDATES'` and copied into ~250 programs as part of the standard calling convention documented in that copybook's header comment ΓÇö 232 files call `CALL IMMDATES-PGM-NAME USING IMMDATES-PARM`.
(3) Indirect calls via `WS-IMMDATES`, a program-local PIC X(08)/X(8) field independently declared with `VALUE 'IMMDATES'` in 9 programs (IMM0046, IMM0047, IMM0195, IMM0197, IMM0680, IMM750, IMMMBRC2, IMMMBRCS, IMMOADPR) ΓÇö 7 of those 9 actually issue `CALL WS-IMMDATES`; IMM0046 and IMM0680 declare the constant but call IMMDATES-PGM-NAME instead, so they contribute no WS-IMMDATES call site.
Confirmed no other data-name is ever assigned the literal 'IMMDATES' (checked all VALUE clauses and all MOVE '...' TO statements containing that literal) and that IMMDATES-PGM-NAME/WS-IMMDATES are never reassigned at runtime (set once via VALUE clause only) ΓÇö so every listed call resolves unconditionally to the IMMDATES subprogram; there is no risk of these fields pointing elsewhere at runtime. Ruled out false positives: comment lines (`*` in column 7) mentioning "CALL IMMDATES", DISPLAY literals like 'FAILED TO CALL IMMDATES', error-message text such as 'IMMDATES FUNCTION INVALID', and the field IMMIOED-TBL-ERR-NAME (used only to record an error label, never called). Copybook IMMDATED.CPY's 88-level condition names are all status/function codes, not call-target aliases. Inclusion-exclusion cross-check on the three sets (11 literal, 232 via IMMDATES-PGM-NAME, 7 via WS-IMMDATES, with a 4-file overlap between literal/PGM-NAME and a 2-file overlap between WS-IMMDATES/PGM-NAME) confirms the union is exactly 244 distinct files, matching a direct combined grep.

structured_output.justification: Searched every .COB/.CPY file under COBOL/ for the string IMMDATES (8688 raw hits in 284 files), then narrowed to actual CALL statements with the pattern CALL ['\"]IMMDATES['\"] | CALL <token containing IMMDATES>, which isolates real invocations from mere data-structure/field references (most of the 284 files just COPY the IMMDATES-PARM layout from COPYBOOKS\\IMMDATED.CPY without calling it). That narrower search returned 241 files. Two were excluded after manual inspection: COPYBOOKS\\IMMDATED.CPY only contains the copybook's own documentation comments showing example CALL syntax (col-7 '*' comment lines) ΓÇö it has no executable CALL itself, it just supplies the IMMDATES-PARM record and the constant IMMDATES-PGM-NAME (PIC X(08) VALUE 'IMMDATES') that callers use; and PROGRAMS\\IMM9430.COB has its only CALL IMMDATES-PGM-NAME line entirely commented out (dead code, verified by reading lines 619-636), so it never actually calls the subprogram at runtime. That leaves 239 files with a genuine call to IMMDATES. Two call styles were found: (1) literal ΓÇö CALL 'IMMDATES' USING IMMDATES-PARM, found in 7 files exclusively (IMM0191, IMM0193, IMM3275, IMM5001, IMMFTPCD, IMMHLFE, IMMLIFE) plus mixed into 4 more (IMM0038, IMM3800, IMMMBRC, IMMPXF0, which also have indirect calls elsewhere in the same file); (2) indirect ΓÇö CALL <field> USING IMMDATES-PARM, where <field> is a PIC X(08) working-storage item whose VALUE clause is literally 'IMMDATES'. In the large majority of files this field is IMMDATES-PGM-NAME, copied in from COPYBOOKS\\IMMDATED.CPY (line: 05 IMMDATES-PGM-NAME PIC X(08) VALUE 'IMMDATES'.). A small set of older programs instead declare their own local equivalent, WS-IMMDATES PIC X(08) VALUE 'IMMDATES' (IMM0047, IMM0195, IMM0197, IMM750, IMM0680, IMMOADPR, and, alongside IMMDATES-PGM-NAME, IMMMBRC2/IMMMBRCS) ΓÇö functionally identical indirection, just a differently named field. No other indirection mechanism (e.g., a generic dynamically-built program-name variable unrelated to the IMMDATES name) was found; a MOVE 'IMMDATES' TO IMMIOED-TBL-ERR-NAME in IMMIOED.COB was checked and confirmed to be only an error-logging label, not a call target. Since the parameter list is not changing, both call styles resolve to the same physical subprogram and are equally affected by an internal logic change to IMMDATES.

Grepped for three call patterns across *.COB (excluding the copybook itself, which only contains the pattern in comments/field definitions): (1) literal `CALL 'IMMDATES'` ΓÇö 11 files; (2) indirect `CALL IMMDATES-PGM-NAME` ΓÇö 228 files; (3) a second, locally-redeclared indirect field pattern `05 WS-IMMDATES PIC X(08) VALUE 'IMMDATES'` used as `CALL WS-IMMDATES` ΓÇö found in 7 files (2 of which, IMMMBRC2/IMMMBRCS, also call via IMMDATES-PGM-NAME elsewhere; IMM0046 and IMM0680 declare WS-IMMDATES but never call it, so they were excluded from that category and counted only under IMMDATES-PGM-NAME). structured_output.justification: Searched the whole COBOL/ tree (291 files reference the string "IMMDATES" in some form). Classified matches into: (1) literal calls, found via CALL 'IMMDATES'/CALL "IMMDATES" (regex CALL\s+['\"]IMMDATES['\"]) ΓÇö 11 files; (2) indirect calls, found via CALL IMMDATES-PGM-NAME or CALL WS-IMMDATES. The copybook COPYBOOKS/IMMDATED.CPY defines 05 IMMDATES-PGM-NAME PIC X(08) VALUE 'IMMDATES' inside the IMMDATES-PARM structure, and its own header comments instruct callers to do CALL IMMDATES-PGM-NAME USING IMMDATES-PARM ΓÇö every program that COPYs this copybook and issues that CALL is an indirect call through that field. A handful of programs (IMM0047, IMM0195, IMM0197, IMM750, IMMMBRC2, IMMMBRCS, IMMOADPR) additionally/instead declare their own working-storage field WS-IMMDATES PIC X(08) VALUE 'IMMDATES' and CALL WS-IMMDATES ΓÇö also indirect, just via a locally-named field. Verified with grep for CALL\s+IMMDATES-PGM-NAME|CALL\s+WS-IMMDATES (233 files), then manually excluded false positives: COPYBOOKS/IMMDATED.CPY itself (the matches are only in its instructional comment block, not executable code), IMM9430.COB (its only match is inside a fully commented-out paragraph, i.e. no live call), and non-call text incidentally containing the string (e.g. a DISPLAY 'FAILED TO CALL IMMDATES...' literal in IMM0651.COB, and comment banners like '* THIS PARAGRAPH WILL CALL IMMDATES SUBROUTINE...' in IMMANNVU/IMMANVIO/IMMANVRS, IMMRTCC, IMMSBDU, IMMEGFS ΓÇö all of these files still count because they also contain genuine, non-comment CALL statements elsewhere). Also checked WS-IMMDATES fields declared in IMM0046.COB and IMM0680.COB and confirmed they are dead/unused (never appear as the operand of a CALL) ΓÇö those two files call only via IMMDATES-PGM-NAME. Also searched MOVE 'IMMDATES' TO ... to rule out other runtime-assigned indirect targets; the only hits (IMMIOED.COB) move the literal into an error-message field for diagnostics, not a CALL target. Result: 11 literal-call files, 232 indirect-call files, with 4 files (IMM0038.COB, IMM3800.COB, IMMMBRC.COB, IMMPXF0.COB) containing both a literal CALL 'IMMDATES' and an indirect CALL IMMDATES-PGM-NAME, giving 239 distinct files and 243 call-site entries.

Cross-referenced with a `VALUE 'IMMDATES'` search to confirm the two field names used to hold the program name at runtime: IMMDATES-PGM-NAME (declared in COPYBOOKS\IMMDATED.CPY and pulled in via COPY) and a locally-declared WS-IMMDATES (in IMM0047, IMM0195, IMM0197, IMM750, IMMMBRC2, IMMMBRCS, IMMOADPR; also declared but unused in IMM0046 and IMM0680, which actually call via IMMDATES-PGM-NAME). Also searched for `MOVE 'IMMDATES' TO` to rule out a generic/dynamic-dispatch field pattern (found none ΓÇö the one hit, in IMMIOED.COB, populates an error-logging field, not a call target, confirmed by reading that file's surrounding code). Manually excluded: (1) COPYBOOKS\IMMDATED.CPY's own CALL lines, which are comment/documentation text inside the copybook's header block, not executable code; (2) PROGRAMS\IMM9430.COB, whose sole CALL IMMDATES-PGM-NAME line is commented out (indicator-column *); (3) IMM0651.COB line 1670, a DISPLAY of the literal string 'FAILED TO CALL IMMDATES -----' (an error message, not a call) ΓÇö that file still counts via its real call at line 1665; (4) similar descriptive/comment lines in IMMANNVU, IMMANVIO, IMMANVRS, IMMEGFS, IMMRTCC, IMMSBDU that mention "CALL IMMDATES" in prose or commented-out code but are backed by genuine active calls elsewhere in the same file.

structured_output.justification: Started from `grep -rn "CALL" PROGRAMS/*.COB | grep -i "IMMDATES"` (~1300 raw hits across ~100+ files initially flagged by a broader filename/text search), then filtered out false positives: comment lines (banner text like "* CALLING MODULES - IMMDATES" or "THIS PARAGRAPH WILL CALL IMMDATES..."), COBOL paragraph names/PERFORM statements whose label merely contains "CALL-IMMDATES" (e.g. `PERFORM 90000-CALL-IMMDATES THRU 90000-EXIT` / paragraph header `90000-CALL-IMMDATES.` ΓÇö these PERFORM an internal paragraph, not the external subprogram), DISPLAY/MOVE string literals mentioning IMMDATES, and data-name fields (PIC clauses) whose name happens to include IMMDATES. Only lines where the actual COBOL CALL verb's target is the literal 'IMMDATES' or a data-name resolving to it were kept. Two indirect call-target variables exist in the codebase: IMMDATES-PGM-NAME (defined once in COPYBOOKS/IMMDATED.CPY as `PIC X(08) VALUE 'IMMDATES'`, copied into most IMM* programs, never reassigned anywhere) and WS-IMMDATES (independently declared with the same VALUE 'IMMDATES' in 9 programs: IMM0046, IMM0047, IMM0195, IMM0197, IMM0680, IMM750, IMMMBRC2, IMMMBRCS, IMMOADPR ΓÇö also never reassigned, though IMM0046/IMM0680 declare it but don't actually call through it, using IMMDATES-PGM-NAME instead). No other dynamic call-target variable pointing to IMMDATES was found. COPYBOOKS/IMMDATED.CPY itself and IMM9430.COB (whose only reference is inside a fully commented-out dead paragraph) contain no real call sites and are excluded. Verified no lowercase variants and no split CALL-verb/target-on-next-line statements exist. Result: 239 distinct files with 624 total individual call sites; 11 of those files contain at least one literal `CALL 'IMMDATES'` (7 purely literal: IMM0191, IMM0193, IMM3275, IMM5001, IMMFTPCD, IMMHLFE, IMMLIFE; 4 mixing literal and indirect calls in the same file: IMM0038, IMM3800, IMMMBRC, IMMPXF0), and the remaining 228 files call exclusively through the named field (IMMDATES-PGM-NAME or WS-IMMDATES). No CAST Imaging MCP tool was available in this session, so the analysis was done via direct static search of the COBOL/COBOL source tree instead.

Methodology:
1. Read COPYBOOKS/IMMDATED.CPY, which defines the standard call parameter block IMMDATES-PARM and, within it, field IMMDATES-PGM-NAME PIC X(08) VALUE 'IMMDATES' ΓÇö the field most programs use for an indirect call (CALL IMMDATES-PGM-NAME USING IMMDATES-PARM).
2. Searched the whole tree for VALUE 'IMMDATES' / VALUE "IMMDATES" to enumerate every field capable of holding the program name at runtime. Besides the copybook's IMMDATES-PGM-NAME, found one other recurring locally-declared field name, WS-IMMDATES PIC X(08) VALUE 'IMMDATES', used by a small subset of programs (IMM0047, IMM0195, IMM0197, IMM750, IMMOADPR, IMMMBRC2, IMMMBRCS) instead of, or in addition to, the copybook field. Confirmed no COPY IMMDATED REPLACING usage exists anywhere, so no other renamed variants of the field are possible.
3. Since every real call (literal or indirect) in this codebase passes the same argument, USING IMMDATES-PARM, on the same line, searching for that exact string reliably surfaces every genuine call site regardless of which program-name form precedes it, including cases where CALL and the program-name field are split across a continuation line. This produced 239 files; excluded IMMDATES.COB itself (its PROCEDURE DIVISION USING IMMDATES-PARM header, i.e. the subprogram's own definition, not a call) and COPYBOOKS/IMMDATED.CPY (the string only appears in its embedded usage-instruction comments), leaving 237 genuine caller files.
4. Cross-checked all comment-only or dead-code false positives: files that only COPY IMMDATED without ever referencing any IMMDATES-* field or CALL statement (e.g. IMM0039, IMM0044, IMMAUBL and the rest of the IMMAU* family, IMM0500/IMM0510/IMM0640/IMM0761/IMM0771, IMMGRPL, IMMGRTA, IMMHCDHS, IMMHCRM, IMMIBKI, IMMIDMA/C/I, IMMIEDD, IMMIZPI, IMMRTDI, IMMSUBN, IMMEGCI/IMMEGCIS/IMMEGLI/IMMEGPU, IMMEMBNS/IMMEMEDS/IMMENRNS/IMMERRHS/IMMBNTA/IMMDADI/IMMEAUD/IMMGBKI, etc.) were excluded ΓÇö verified individually that they contain no CALL statement to the subprogram, only comments, error-message text literals, or an unused copied data structure. IMMIOED.COB's 'MOVE 'IMMDATES' TO IMMIOED-TBL-ERR-NAME' lines are error-log labels, not call targets ΓÇö its real call is via IMMDATES-PGM-NAME.
5. Classified each of the 237 caller files as literal (CALL 'IMMDATES' ... ) or indirect (CALL <field> ...) by checking each file's actual CALL statements. Four files use both mechanisms in different call sites (IMMPXF0.COB, IMMMBRC.COB, IMM3800.COB, IMM0038.COB) and appear twice in the calls list, once per style. Seven files call it only literally. The remaining 226 files call it only indirectly ΓÇö 219 via the copybook's IMMDATES-PGM-NAME, 5 via a locally-declared WS-IMMDATES (IMM0047, IMM0195, IMM0197, IMM750, IMMOADPR), and 2 via both field names in different call sites (IMMMBRC2, IMMMBRCS; both still reported as a single 'indirect' entry since the call_style itself doesn't change).
6. All 237 files reside in the PROGRAMS/ directory; no calls to IMMDATES exist under API/, PROG-BATCH/, or PROG-CICS/.
